visually related to the pre-war Antonov AN-BK-1 Horlytsia design
Strength: Larger airframe allows more range/payload than smaller purpose-built loitering-style long-range drones
Limitation: Higher apparent unit cost due to more sophisticated light-aircraft construction, versus the deliberately cheap, disposable design philosophy of types like AQ-400 Scythe
Estimated quantity available: Production status confirmed; exact numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: Confirmed as an Antonov/Ukroboronprom design - a state aerospace manufacturer pivoting from traditional aircraft production to drone production after the 2022 invasion, illustrating industrial adaptation under wartime pressure
contrast_vs_traditional: A larger one-way attack airframe with greater payload than the FP or Beaver family, Lyutyy is part of the same shift: deep-strike reach that traditional doctrine priced in missiles or manned sorties is now available as a mass-producible drone, which changes the economics of a defender's interception problem more than it changes the physics of the strike itself.
